title: SEIZURES, EARLY-ONSET, WITH NEURODEGENERATION AND BRAIN CALCIFICATIONS

relationships.phenotype: SEIZURES, EARLY-ONSET, WITH NEURODEGENERATION AND BRAIN CALCIFICATIONS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that early-onset seizures with neurodegeneration and brain calcifications (SENEBAC) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the NRROS gene on chromosome 3q29.

checks.claim: Early-onset seizures with neurodegeneration and brain calcifications (SENEBAC) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the NRROS gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified homozygous NRROS variants in the affected children from both families
checks.explanation: The paper reports only homozygous variants, not compound heterozygous ones. It also does not use the name SENEBAC.

checks.claim: The NRROS gene is located on chromosome 3q29.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we describe a novel early onset lethal encephalopathy due to mutations in the microglial-associated protein NRROS.
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to a gene the paper names.

paragraphs.text: SENEBAC is an autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder. It begins in infancy with seizures and developmental regression, often after early development that seemed normal. Brain imaging shows intracranial calcifications and white matter abnormalities, a picture that can resemble the type I interferonopathies, such as Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome. The disease is progressive and is often fatal in early childhood. It is thought to be a microgliopathy caused by loss of NRROS-dependent activation of TGF-beta-1 in microglia.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Biallelic mutations in NRROS cause an early onset lethal microgliopathy.
checks.explanation: Biallelic (homozygous) mutations, one family with first-cousin parents, which follows directly as recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is a neurodegenerative disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: in the second year of life, they experienced the onset of refractory seizures and neurodegeneration
checks.explanation: The paper describes neurodegeneration.

checks.claim: SENEBAC begins in infancy with seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: the onset of seizures occurred within the first year of life, followed by developmental regression
checks.explanation: Seizures started in the first year of life.

checks.claim: SENEBAC begins in infancy with developmental regression.
checks.evidence_quote: in the second year of life, they experienced the onset of refractory seizures and neurodegeneration
checks.explanation: The paper says neurodegeneration; it does not explicitly mention developmental regression.

checks.claim: In SENEBAC, the onset of seizures and regression often follows early development that seemed normal.
checks.evidence_quote: All three children were born after a normal pregnancy and delivery, and early development was unremarkable. However, in the second year of life, they experienced the onset of refractory seizures
checks.explanation: Early development was normal before onset.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in SENEBAC shows intracranial calcifications.
checks.evidence_quote: Neuroimaging initially demonstrated fine calcification at the depths of the cerebral gyri, with normal white matter
checks.explanation: Calcification is shown on imaging.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in SENEBAC shows white matter abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: repeat imaging revealed increased calcification, severe generalized atrophy with ventricular dilatation, and diffuse signal changes in cerebral and cerebellar white matter
checks.explanation: White matter signal changes are shown on later imaging.

checks.claim: The brain imaging picture in SENEBAC can resemble type I interferonopathies such as Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not compare the imaging to interferonopathies or Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is a progressive disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Follow-up shows rapidly progressive cortical and sub-cortical atrophy in P1 and P3.
checks.explanation: The disease is progressive.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is often fatal in early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: leading to death between the ages of 27 and 36 months
checks.explanation: Death in early childhood.

checks.claim: SENEBAC is thought to be a microgliopathy caused by loss of NRROS-dependent activation of TGF-beta-1 in microglia.
checks.evidence_quote: Functions of NRROS proposed above, notably in ROS and TGFβ regulation, may be important in disease pathogenesis.
checks.explanation: The paper calls the disorder a microgliopathy, but it only raises TGFβ (and ROS) regulation as possible mechanisms; it does not state that loss of TGF-beta-1 activation is the cause.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2020) and Dong et al. (2020) reported patients from unrelated families with biallelic NRROS mutations. Seizures began in infancy and were followed by loss of developmental milestones, progressive neurologic deterioration and early death. Brain imaging showed intracranial calcifications and white matter changes. Neuropathologic examination showed loss of homeostatic microglial markers, such as P2RY12 and TMEM119, together with neurodegeneration.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) reported patients from unrelated families with biallelic NRROS mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Patients 1 (P1) and P2, both females, were the first and third children of non-consanguineous parents of Maori descent (family F1442), whilst P3 (family F2382), a male, was the first child of first cousin south Asian parents
checks.explanation: Two unrelated families, both with biallelic variants.

checks.claim: Dong et al. (2020) reported patients from unrelated families with biallelic NRROS mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We report six individuals from four families with bi-allelic variants in NRROS.
checks.explanation: The abstract says there were four families but does not say they were unrelated.

checks.claim: In the patients with biallelic NRROS mutations, seizures began in infancy.
checks.evidence_quote: the onset of seizures occurred within the first year of life
checks.explanation: Seizures began in infancy.

checks.claim: In the patients with biallelic NRROS mutations, seizure onset was followed by loss of developmental milestones.
checks.evidence_quote: the onset of seizures occurred within the first year of life, followed by developmental regression
checks.explanation: Developmental regression followed the seizures.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic NRROS mutations had progressive neurologic deterioration.
checks.evidence_quote: Follow-up shows rapidly progressive cortical and sub-cortical atrophy in P1 and P3.
checks.explanation: The deterioration was progressive.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic NRROS mutations died early.
checks.evidence_quote: leading to death between the ages of 27 and 36 months
checks.explanation: The patients died early.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in the patients with biallelic NRROS mutations showed intracranial calcifications.
checks.evidence_quote: demonstrate widespread spot and linear calcification in the deep and sub-cortical white matter
checks.explanation: Calcifications are seen on CT.

checks.claim: Brain imaging in the patients with biallelic NRROS mutations showed white matter changes.
checks.evidence_quote: diffuse signal changes in cerebral and cerebellar white matter
checks.explanation: White matter changes are reported.

checks.claim: Neuropathologic examination of patients with biallelic NRROS mutations showed loss of homeostatic microglial markers, such as P2RY12 and TMEM119.
checks.evidence_quote: The present case showed disruption to the distribution, density, and cell morphology of IBA1 cells alongside loss of P2Y12 staining and weak TMEM119 immunoreactivity, indicative of marked parenchymal microglial abnormalities.
checks.explanation: P2Y12 staining was lost and TMEM119 staining was weak.

checks.claim: Neuropathologic examination of patients with biallelic NRROS mutations showed neurodegeneration.
checks.evidence_quote: There was widespread neuronal loss with reactive gliosis throughout the grey matter
checks.explanation: Neuropathology showed neuronal loss.

paragraphs.text: The reported patients carried homozygous or compound heterozygous NRROS mutations, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The reported SENEBAC patients carried homozygous or compound heterozygous NRROS mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified homozygous NRROS variants in the affected children from both families
checks.explanation: Only homozygous variants are reported; there are no compound heterozygous cases in this paper.

checks.claim: The homozygous or compound heterozygous NRROS mutations in SENEBAC patients are consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: Biallelic mutations in NRROS cause an early onset lethal microgliopathy.
checks.explanation: The biallelic (homozygous) variants fit recessive inheritance, but the paper does not state the inheritance mode and reports no compound heterozygotes.

paragraphs.text: Smith et al. (2020) and Dong et al. (2020) used exome sequencing to find biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the NRROS gene in affected children. The mutations segregated with the disorder in the families studied. Functional studies suggested that the mutations impaired the ability of NRROS to anchor latent TGF-beta-1 at the cell surface and support its activation.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2020) used exome sequencing to find biallelic loss-of-function NRROS mutations in affected children.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome sequencing identified homozygous NRROS variants in the affected children from both families: a c.1777C > T/p.(Gln593*) and a c.1257del/p.(Gly420AlafsTer14) in F1442 and F2382, respectively.
checks.explanation: Both variants are predicted to truncate the protein, i.e. loss of function.

checks.claim: Dong et al. (2020) used exome sequencing to find biallelic loss-of-function NRROS mutations in affected children.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic LoF NRROS Variants Impairing Active TGF-β1 Delivery Cause a Severe Infantile-Onset Neurodegenerative Condition
checks.explanation: The title confirms bi-allelic loss-of-function variants, but the abstract does not say exome sequencing was used. That method may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: The biallelic NRROS mutations segregated with the disorder in the families studied.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper does not describe segregation analysis in the families.

checks.claim: Functional studies suggested that the NRROS mutations impaired the ability of NRROS to anchor latent TGF-beta-1 at the cell surface.
checks.evidence_quote: These variants result in aberrant NRROS proteins with impaired ability to anchor latent TGF-β1 on the cell surface.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: Functional studies suggested that the NRROS mutations impaired the ability of NRROS to support TGF-beta-1 activation.
checks.evidence_quote: this anchoring is required for activation of TGF-β1 in macrophages and microglia
checks.explanation: Impaired activation is inferred from the loss of anchoring, which the paper says is needed for activation, and the title mentions impaired 'Active TGF-β1 Delivery'. The abstract reports no direct test of activation.

paragraphs.text: In mice, Nrros deficiency disrupted microglial TGF-beta-1 signaling. Microglia lost their homeostatic signature, and the mice developed neurologic disease with neurodegeneration (Qin et al., 2018).

checks.claim: In mice, Nrros deficiency disrupted microglial TGF-beta-1 signaling (Qin et al., 2018).
checks.evidence_quote: Reported functions include the regulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production through control of NOX2 stability, responsiveness of Toll-like receptor signaling, and processing/activation of transforming growth factor (TGF)-β via physical interactions with the latent complex.
checks.explanation: The paper mentions NRROS's role in TGFβ activation, but it does not explicitly state that Nrros-deficient mice had disrupted microglial TGFβ signaling.

checks.claim: In Nrros-deficient mice, microglia lost their homeostatic signature (Qin et al., 2018).
checks.evidence_quote: Both Nrros−/− mouse studies observed a loss of homeostatic gene expression profile which included suppression of P2ry12 and Tmem119 expression
checks.explanation: The homeostatic signature was lost in the mice.

checks.claim: Nrros-deficient mice developed neurologic disease with neurodegeneration (Qin et al., 2018).
checks.evidence_quote: Nrros−/−mice exhibited progressive neurological decline, including motor defects and abnormal locomotor activity, from age 2–3 months and death by 6 months of age. Neuropathology in these mouse models includes neuronal loss, demyelination, axonal pathology
checks.explanation: The mice had neurological disease with neuronal loss.
